summary:
This is a Senate amendment to the House amendment to S. 2073, substituting the entire text and retitling the bill the "Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act." The measure comprises three titles addressing minors' online safety, children's and teens' online privacy, and agency reporting requirements. Section 112 sets a general effective date of 18 months after enactment for Subtitle A of Title I unless otherwise provided.

**Title I, Subtitle A (Kids Online Safety).** Sections 101–113 impose obligations on "covered platforms"—online platforms, online video games, messaging applications, or video streaming services reasonably likely to be used by minors (defined as individuals under 17; "child" is under 13), with enumerated exceptions (common carriers, broadband, email, certain messaging/conferencing services, nonprofits, schools, libraries, news/sports apps, B2B software, and VPNs). Section 102 establishes a "duty of care" requiring reasonable care in designing features to prevent enumerated harms (specified mental-health disorders, compulsive use, violence/bullying, sexual exploitation, marketing of narcotics/tobacco/gambling/alcohol, and deceptive marketing), subject to a limitation preserving minors' independent searches. Section 103 mandates safeguards, default most-protective settings, parental tools (enabled by default for children), reporting mechanisms with tiered response deadlines (10/21 days by user count; imminent-threat immediacy), a dark-patterns prohibition, and advertising restrictions. Sections 104–105 require disclosures and, for platforms exceeding 10,000,000 monthly U.S. users, annual public transparency reports based on independent third-party audits. Sections 106–108 direct FTC contracts with the National Academy (using FTC Act §6(b) authority, 15 U.S.C. 46(b)), market-research guidance, and a Commerce/FCC/FTC age-verification study (report due 1 year). Section 110 treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under FTC Act §18(a)(1)(B) and authorizes state attorney-general enforcement for §§103–105 (not §102). Section 111 establishes a Kids Online Safety Council, exempt from FACA. Section 113 preserves FERPA, COPPA, FTC Act §18(h), and §230, and disclaims any age-verification mandate.

**Subtitle B (§§120–121)** requires operators of online platforms using an "opaque algorithm" to provide notices and enable an "input-transparent algorithm" option, enforced as an FTC Act unfair/deceptive practice, effective 1 year after enactment. **Subtitle C (§§130–131)** provides conflict-only preemption (permitting greater state protections) and severability.

**Title II (§§201–204)** substantially amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 6501 et seq.), extending coverage to "teens" (13–16), broadening "operator" and "personal information," adding a "knowledge fairly implied" standard, restricting individual-specific advertising, adding deletion/correction rights, and directing FTC guidance and studies (including a GAO fintech-privacy study).

**Title III (§301)** amends 31 U.S.C. 1125 (and conforming provisions of 31 U.S.C. 1105(a) and the James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023) to require agencies to identify outdated or duplicative recurring reports in budget justification materials, with recommendations to sunset, modify, or consolidate them.

The bill contains authorizations and directives but no explicit appropriation. The title is amended to "An Act to protect the safety and privacy of children on the internet."
